name: fragment-varying-depth-to-float4
rationale: The fragment entry expands its perspective center scalar float varying to (depth,depth,depth,1); the generated fullscreen vertex stage supplies the value and the selected RGBA32Float pixel captures the result byte-exactly.

name: srgb-decode-at-the-two-fixed-points-of-a-half-power
rationale:
Metal's half powr cannot be pinned byte-exactly at a general argument - the precise variant Metal runs and the fast:: variant SPIRV-Cross reaches for a half operand differ by about one half ULP - so this case lands on the two arguments where every implementation has to agree, and uses the third channel to prove the power was applied at all.

The shader is an sRGB decode over a framebuffer-fetch colour: below 0.0404 the channel is scaled by 1/12.92, above it the channel is offset by 0.055, scaled by 1/1.055 and raised to 2.4. Red is 1.0: the offset-and-scale rounds back to exactly 1.0 in half (1.0546875 * 0.9482421875 is 1.0000991821, which is a tenth of a half ULP above one), and powr is one at one for any implementation. Green is 1024: the same chain gives exactly 971, and 971^2.4 is 1.5e7, two hundred times over the half maximum, so it overflows to infinity with room that no implementation error can close. Blue is 0.03125, which is under the threshold, so it takes the linear branch instead - 0.03125 * 0.077392578125 is exactly 0.0024185180664, a half - and that is what makes red and green evidence about powr rather than about a select that collapsed. Alpha passes through untouched.

The two integers in the uniform buffer are both zero, which selects the transfer function and makes the depth output alpha-divide: the float depth attachment holds 0.25 and alpha is 0.5, so the written depth is 0.5. The eight output bytes were derived by hand first; Metal and MoltenVK both answer them.

Covers air.powr.v3f16 (79 uncovered sources) and is the first authored case anywhere to read a render target back as a fragment input - framebuffer fetch - or to write a fragment depth.

name: walk-a-device-pointer-chain-through-a-loop-phi
rationale: A loop-carried phi of device pointers whose backedge arm is a pointer LOADED out of device memory -- the shape emit_bda_address_phi exists for, and one no authored case reached. The Node struct's device-pointer member makes the frontend emit root as an air.indirect_buffer with a nested air.buffer, so cur->next is a real load of a ptr addrspace(1) from device memory, and because that load sits behind the loop header, bda_phi_address_id has to reserve the address of a pointer it has not lowered yet. Reserving the load's own SSA result there emitted an OpIAdd %ulong over an id nothing defines; 6f20d398 reserves bda_address_name(name) instead, and this case is the device evidence. The walk is real and terminates: root.next points at a second node whose own next is null, and the null guard keeps cur on the last valid node instead of dereferencing zero. steps = 2 is the case-supplied literal that bounds the loop, so the sum visits node 0 (7) then node 1 (11) and the trailing read adds node 1 again: 7 + 11 + 11 = 29 in every lane, independent of thread id, on both backends.

name: a-bound-constraint-texture-is-not-the-null-texture
rationale: The kernel guards on the destination array's own width, height and array size, dots a guide texel against a coefficient texel, adds a second coefficient's red, and then asks whether the constraint texture is the null texture. The case binds a real constraint texture, so the answer is false and the shader takes the longer arm: it samples the constraints, reads the destination back through its own read_write binding, and interpolates between the destination's prior value and the dotted value by the constraint weight. A lowering that answered true instead would take the short arm and write 2.25 where this writes 6.125, so the null query is what the compared texel reports. The four dot products are each exactly one half, so the sum is 2.0 under every association fast-math could choose, and the final multiply-add is exact whether or not it contracts.

name: constant-uint-255
rationale: The fragment entry ignores its position input and returns literal uint 255 at color location zero; one full-coverage fragment must replace the exact poisoned R32Uint pixel.

name: decompose-a-z-index-behind-sixty-bytes-of-uniform
rationale: The only thing that decides where each of the four threads reads and writes is IntegerDivisionParams, and that struct sits at byte 60 of the constant buffer and is reached ONLY as a member pointer handed to a two-block helper. Divisor two and shift zero split gid.z into quotient and remainder, source_strides {_,_,2,1} turn that pair back into the linear index z, and result_strides {_,2,8,4} scatter thread z to floats 4z..4z+3 with no two threads overlapping, so the whole 64-byte output is exactly the four source floats each repeated four times. If the helper reads its parameter as zeros the kernel writes nothing at all: source_width would be zero and every thread would fail its first bounds check.

name: linked-single-unit-matrix-multiply-reduction
rationale: The scalar callback specialization has M=N=K=B=1, one four-byte row and matrix, one batch and tile in every dimension, and exactly one K split. Those literal unit fields bound the sole reduction loop to one iteration. The input float is one and the exact linked scalar destination writes the reduced value to the sole poisoned device-array output; the float4 callback remains linked for the structurally present alternate lane shape.

name: fragment-varying-half4-with-viewport
rationale: The fragment returns its perspective center half4 varying unchanged while structurally accepting an unused viewport index; the generated fullscreen draw captures the color byte-exactly.

name: linked-single-unit-average-tmp-output
rationale: Every source, destination, kernel, stride, dilation, threadgroup cube, and group-count extent is exactly one with zero offsets. The required multi-destination constants declare one float source at table element zero and one active float destination at element one, so the small-parameter average path executes only its unit window and bounded single invocation before writing exact one.

name: linked-single-threadgroup-zero-bin
rationale: One 1x1 threadgroup dispatches one invocation. kLogBinEntries=0 makes both initialization and flush loops contain exactly one bin, kTGSizeIs256=false uses the literal one-thread group size as their stride, and source_size=1x1 bounds the image path. The exact linked callback returns float4 zero without dereferencing resources; the poisoned global bin makes the local-atomic aggregation observable byte-exactly.

name: manual-short4-fetch-at-an-offset-transformed-onto-three-of-four-pixels
rationale: Reaching variant of this entry's manual-vertex-fetch case (TODO 6.2, WP-RVC), whose zero constants gave a degenerate position. Constant 132 enables manual fetch; table slot 0 holds the same-library callback re::vertexfetch::fetchFromShort4, and record 0 of the vertex-argument buffer (15 records of 24 bytes, the rest null) points at short4 positions with stride 8 and offset 8, which skips a leading decoy vertex (40, 40, 40). The three positions are (-1, -1), (3, -1), (-1, 3) with z = 1 (short4) with the matrix z scale 1/2, so world z = 5/8. The instance matrix (objectToCrWorld, column-major) scales x and y by 1/2, scales z and translates by (-1/4, -1/4, 1/8); crWorldToProjArray[0] keeps x, y and w and maps z to z/2 + 1/16, so the clip triangle is (-3/4, -3/4), (5/4, -3/4), (-3/4, 5/4) at w = 1. It covers the pixel centres (-1/2, 1/2), (-1/2, -1/2) and (1/2, -1/2) of the 2x2 target with a margin of at least 1/4 from every edge and misses (1/2, 1/2): pixel (1, 0) keeps its fill. The depth is the same at all three vertices, so its interpolation is exact; every product and sum is a small dyadic value, exact in float with or without contraction, and the observer writes (x + 1/2, y + 1/2, z, 1) for each covered pixel. This entry applies no depth bias (screenSpaceDepthBias = 1/4 is authored but unread): depth 0.375.

name: manual-vertex-fetch-null-buffer-defaults
no_effect: Zero instance and view constants give a degenerate position: the primitive covers no fragment, so the render target keeps its authored bytes.
rationale: Function constant 132 enables manual vertex fetch. Every zero-initialized embedded vertex-buffer pointer is null, so each AIR guard bypasses its table lookup and supplies the defined default attribute. Slot zero is the exact same-library invalid-format callback that supplies the table's required type but is unreachable. Zero transform constants produce a deterministic degenerate position. Buffer 30 and its reflected offset-zero device buffer are now authored explicitly; the invalid-format callback deterministically supplies the same default attribute when that first record is reached.

name: vertex-position-depth-zero
rationale: The vertex entry preserves authored x/y, forces clip-space z to zero and w to one, and the typed position observer captures the resulting full-coverage triangle.

name: decode-a-padded-byte-row-into-an-rgba8-uint-texture
rationale: The kernel indexes a device uchar buffer by bytesPerRow*y+x and writes uint4(byte, 0, 0, 255) through air.write_texture_2d.i16.u.v4i32, whose ushort2 coordinate and uint4 payload are both under test. A row stride of 4 over a 2-wide image leaves two decoy bytes per row, so honouring the constant stride is the only way to reach 10/20/30/40; the constant 255 alpha arrives as an i8 -1 that only an unsigned widening turns into 255 rather than a wrap.

name: visible-table-clear-slots-two-through-twenty-seven-threadgroup-primary
rationale: One invocation calls visible-function-table slots 2 through 27 and receives exact float4 zero from all twenty-six linked _uber_clear bodies. A twenty-nine-word size table and eight explicit argument-info records keep every selector and offset in bounds; register 2 is selected. The single-invocation threadgroup executes both barriers over internal static storage and writes the linked result to the poisoned primary texel byte-exactly.

name: visible-table-clear-slots-two-through-eight-threadgroup-primary
rationale: One invocation calls visible-function-table slots 2 through 8 and receives exact float4 zero from all seven linked _uber_clear bodies. A ten-word size table and eight explicit argument-info records keep every selector and offset in bounds; register 2 is selected. The single-invocation threadgroup executes both barriers over internal static storage and writes the linked result to the poisoned primary texel byte-exactly.

name: thirty-two-simdgroups-fold-four-texels-into-one-atomic-float-add
rationale: The dispatch is one 1024-thread threadgroup, which is exactly 32 simdgroups on this device, and that is what closes the kernel's two-stage reduction. Stage one has every thread sample the texture at its own thread_position_in_grid through the module's pixel-coordinate clamp_to_zero sampler; the texture is 4x1, so threads 0 to 3 read the four texels and threads 4 to 1023 read the zero the address mode returns, which also makes the case indifferent to whether a pixel coordinate names the texel at floor(u) or one either side of it -- a one-texel shift still covers the same four texels. Stage two has lane 0 of each simdgroup park its simd_sum in a 32-entry threadgroup array and simdgroup 0 sum that array back. The array is undef on entry and Metal zero-fills no threadgroup memory, so any dispatch with fewer than 32 simdgroups would sum entries no thread ever wrote; 1024 threads is the smallest -- and here the only -- threadgroup size that fills it. Which threads land in which simdgroup does not matter, because the outer sum is over all 1024 either way. Both reductions are float sums, so the case is only exact if their order cannot matter: the components are the integers 1 through 12, summing to 78 with squares summing to 650, all far inside binary32's exactly representable integers, so every association agrees bit for bit. The buffer starts at (100, 200) and the two air.atomic.global.add.f32 calls leave (178, 850), a pair neither the initial contents nor either reduction alone can produce.

name: float4-to-half4-varying-conversion
rationale: The generated companion supplies a finite float4 perspective varying; the fragment converts every lane to half and writes the result byte-exactly.

name: empty-kernel-execution
rationale: The entry has no parameters, no writable reflected resources, and a single return; one invocation must complete successfully and its exact observable output is the empty byte sequence.

name: saturate-tanh-in-both-directions-around-its-zero
rationale: Every bn_params lane is (scale 1, bias 0, mean 0, sigma 1), so the normalization is the identity and air.fast_tanh.v4f32 sees exactly the authored half4. fused_relu is off and fused_tanh is on, so the tanh arm is the only one taken. Lane zero pins tanh's fixed point at zero; the +-10 lanes are far enough into saturation that every approximation of tanh lands within half a ULP of half precision from one, so the stored half4 is (0, 1, -1, 1) exactly while the case still distinguishes the sign and the saturation.

name: linked-k48-quantized-matrix-multiply-half-16-transposed
rationale: Reaching variant of the zero-K case of this entry (DESIGN D296; WP-EVG, TODO 6.2), whose K = 0 stops the kernel before its arithmetic. One threadgroup of 32 lanes (1 simdgroup) runs the single 16x16 output tile: B = 1, M = N = 16, K = 48, so the tile is full in M and N (the unsafe loader path) and K runs one whole 32-deep block and a 16-deep remainder (the safe loader). The user constant keeps 8-bit unsigned weights, group size one, no bias, the non-cooperative loader; constant 122 binds a two-entry table (1 source, 1 destination). x is [M][K] (x_ld = 48) and every row holds 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 repeating, so every row of the result is the same: the linked destination callback, which writes table entry 1 at the column coordinate only, stores one value per column from every row, the same value, so the 16 words observed (offset 0, 64 bytes) do not depend on write order. W[n][k] (row stride w_ld = 48 bytes) holds q(n, k) = (11n + 3k + floor(3nk/5)) mod 16, nonlinear in n, so the column sums differ (all 16 distinct whichever scale element the layout reads) and a column computed from another column's weights changes its word; scales and biases (scales_ld = biases_ld = 1, sized N*K) repeat 0.5, 1, 2 and 0, 1, 2, 3 (biases unread without the bias bit). Each dequantized weight is q * s, a multiple of 0.5 at most 30, exact in half and in the threadgroup tile; each product with x is a multiple of 0.5 at most 150 and each sum of 48 at most 7200, below 2^13: exact in float in any order or contraction, and on the half inputs.

name: linked-zero-k-quantized-matrix-multiply-half-16-transposed
no_effect: The authored parameters give the work an empty extent, so the entry returns before any write reaches the selected output.
rationale: A half counterpart of the committed qmm_t_16_float case (DESIGN D272): qmm_t_16_half with the same function constants, resources, one-thread dispatch, and linked visible functions (postfixPrimary_4xf, postfixPrimary_f). Its zero extents keep every loop bound finite, so the case observes the four-byte destination allocation; the kernel links translation units each with its own static initializer and no llvm.global_ctors list, and calls matmul2d, so its translation exercises the unordered-initializer rule (D272.4) and the matmul2d lowering (D272.3). Replaced (DESIGN D296): the linked destination callback writes table entry 1, so the case binds a two-entry table (MPSNDArrayRefSize 1 source, 1 destination) whose destination element carries the source element's fill.

name: a-programmable-blend-over-the-authored-attachment
rationale: Framebuffer fetch as programmable blending (DESIGN D198): one instance of the fullscreen triangle, so each pixel's fragment reads the authored 4x4 rgba32_float attachment once and stores (float4(position.xy, 1, -0.5) + dst) / 2: one rounded sum scaled by a power of two, exact for the dyadic lanes authored, and +inf and -inf lanes stay infinite. Pins the load of the attachment's contents (MTLLoadActionLoad) and the read of the fragment's own pixel.

name: four-overlapping-blends-in-draw-order
rationale: Overlapping-fragment ordering of framebuffer fetch (DESIGN D198): the fullscreen triangle drawn as four instances covers every pixel four times, and Metal orders each fragment's fetch after the earlier fragments' writes, so each pixel holds the blend (src + dst) / 2 applied four times in order (dst/16 + src*15/16, exact for the dyadic lanes). A fetch that read the attachment before an earlier instance wrote it leaves a pixel with fewer applications. The engine's candidate runs it under rasterization-order color attachment access; the old engine's candidate does not order (framebuffer_fetch_overlap).

name: per-sample-blend-at-4x
rationale: Framebuffer fetch in a 4-sample pass (DESIGN D310): does a function that reads [[color(0)]] run once per sample, reading that sample's color? It stores (float4(position.xy, 1, -0.5) + dst) / 2, exact for these lanes. Every sample of the 2x2 rgba32_float target starts distinct (pixel p, sample s: 10p + s, 100 + p, s + 0.25, 1 + s) and every sample is compared, never resolved, so a per-pixel read would give the samples of a pixel one answer, and position.xy shows where each invocation reads [[position]].

name: per-sample-blends-in-order-at-2x
rationale: Framebuffer fetch in a 2-sample pass (DESIGN D310): two overlapping instances, each sample taking two ordered read-modify-writes of (float4(position.xy, 1, -0.5) + dst) / 2. Every sample of the 2x2 rgba32_float target starts distinct (pixel p, sample s: 10p + s, 100 + p, s + 0.25, 1 + s) and every sample is compared, never resolved.

name: per-sample-blends-in-order-at-4x
rationale: Framebuffer fetch in a 4-sample pass (DESIGN D310): three overlapping instances of the fullscreen triangle, so each sample takes three read-modify-writes of (float4(position.xy, 1, -0.5) + dst) / 2 in draw order. Every sample of the 2x2 rgba32_float target starts distinct (pixel p, sample s: 10p + s, 100 + p, s + 0.25, 1 + s) and every sample is compared, never resolved. Pins the per-sample order Metal guarantees.

name: lim8-int4-dequantize-two-codes-per-thread-with-zero-points
rationale: Reaching variant of the zero-limit case of this entry (TODO 6.2, WP-RVC), whose lim = 0 stops every thread before its first load. Eight threads (lim = 8, one threadgroup) each dequantize two adjacent 4-bit codes (loadLen 2 from quantizedFC bits 27 to 32): dim0Div (8, magic 0, shift 3) maps thread t to element 2t of one 16-element row, the other dimensions are 1. The table holds four entries (MPSNDArrayRefSize sums to 4): the packed codes at entry 0 (matrixIndex), the destination at entry 1, four float scales at entry 2 (scaleIndex, isScaleFloat) and four packed 4-bit unsigned zero points at entry 3 (zeropointIndex, isZeroPoint); no minimum value. Dimension 0 takes group attribute 7, so element c reads group c >> log2GroupSize = c >> 2 through the generic (splat) path; dimensions 1 to 3 take attribute 1. Element c is scale[c >> 2] * (q[c] - zp[c >> 2]) with scales 0.5, 2, 1, 4 and nonlinear codes q[c] = ((c^2 + 3c + 1) * 5 + floor(c/3)) mod 16, so a wrong element, group or nibble changes the answer. Codes and zero points convert exactly through half, every difference is a small integer and every scale a power of two, so each result is exact. The identity destination lanes (destIndexFC 0, 1, 2, 3) give the linked writer, which stores table entry 1 at the column coordinate, columns 2t and 2t + 1: each of the 16 observed words is written once. No loop depends on the data: the group-index loop and the lane loops have constant trip counts and lim bounds the threads.

name: linked-zero-limit-i4-dequantize
no_effect: The authored parameters give the work an empty extent, so the entry returns before any write reaches the selected output.
rationale: The exact 240-byte parameter record sets lim to zero. The sole invocation has thread index zero, so the top-level unsigned lim comparison is false and every reachable dequantization and write loop is bypassed. The sole poisoned linked destination remains byte-exact while both retained postfix dependencies are authored explicitly for linkage. Replaced (DESIGN D296): the linked destination callback writes table entry 1, so the case binds a two-entry table (MPSNDArrayRefSize 1 source, 1 destination) whose destination element carries the source element's fill.

name: differentiate-four-linear-quantities-across-a-quad
rationale: Five uncovered fragment-derivative families in one fragment -- air.fwidth.v3f32 (6 case-less corpus sources), air.fwidth.v4f32 (2), air.fwidth.v2f16 (2), air.dfdx.v3f16 (2) and air.dfdy.v3f16 (2), 14 sources. A derivative is the one quantity a fragment case cannot author an input for, being a difference between two lanes of a 2x2 quad. Two things make it exact anyway: [[position]] is gl_FragCoord and not a harness varying, so pos.xy - 0.5 is the integer pixel index with no interpolation in it, and every differentiated expression is LINEAR in that index, so its derivative is a constant the shader states in its own coefficients and coarse and fine derivatives cannot disagree. Every coefficient is a small integer, so every value and difference is exact in binary32 and binary16 alike; the largest half any lane holds is 105. The thirteen non-zero answers are thirteen different integers -- 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 9, 10, 13, 14, 15, -16 -- so a lowering that crossed two components or took an x derivative for a y one lands a number belonging to a different lane of a different call, and the two zeros are the x derivative of a pure-y term and the y derivative of a pure-x term, which a lowering that ignored the axis cannot produce. Sixteen answers do not fit in four channels, so the quad index uint(px) >> 1 selects which four this pixel writes; it is constant across a 2x2 quad so the selection cannot make the quad divergent, and all five derivative calls are made before it. The last channel is dfdx.x + dfdy.y across the two half calls, which is 17 only if both landed.

name: staged-scale-and-bias-of-sixty-four-threads
rationale: The template the indirect-command replay cases dispatch (DESIGN D211), run on its own: params holds the scale 3 and the bias 5, and 64 threads in groups of 8 each stage 3 * (tid + 1) in a 32-byte threadgroup allocation, wait for the group, and write their staged word plus 5, so out[tid] = 3 * tid + 8 (8, 11, ..., 197). Every selected byte differs from the 0xab fill.

name: visible-table-clear-slots-two-through-ten-2x2-output
rationale: One invocation calls visible-function-table slots 2 through 10 and receives exact float4 zero from all nine linked _uber_clear bodies. A twelve-word size table and eight explicit argument-info records keep every selector and offset in bounds; register 2 is selected. The complete 2x2 primary block at origin (2,0) is captured byte-exactly from the poisoned 4x2 resource.

name: custom-callback-zero-state
rationale: A zero shader-state vector disables every optional texture, table, framebuffer-fetch, and dithering branch. The separately linked visible callback returns its incoming half4 unchanged, while zeroed mandatory globals and custom arguments keep every reachable access in bounds. The poisoned one-pixel half4 render target observes the exact linked fragment result.

name: zero-a-counter-tail-with-memset-and-leave-the-fourth-counter-alone
rationale: No authored case reached `llvm.memset.p1.i64`, the device-address-space block fill that four corpus sources use; this 78-line kernel is the smallest and its only non-scalar work is that one call. Each thread writes its own 256-byte `Counter`: six explicit `i32` stores at offsets 0..20 and then `memset(counter.reserved, 0, 232)` at offset 24, which together cover the struct exactly. The buffer starts as 0xAB-style poison -- 0x5A in every one of 1024 bytes -- so a memset that was dropped, short, or written with the wrong fill byte leaves 0x5A where zeros belong and is visible immediately. The case dispatches three threads against a four-`Counter` buffer, so the last 256 bytes must still be entirely 0x5A: that is what shows the fill is bounded by its 232-byte length and its `getelementptr ... i32 6, i64 0` base rather than running to the end of the allocation. The three `args` values 0x11223344, 0xFFFFFFFF and 0x00C0FFEE are byte-asymmetric and distinct, and each lands in field 3 of its own counter, so the per-thread index arithmetic -- `zext i32 tid to i64` used both to load `args[tid]` and to select the counter -- is pinned: a thread reading the wrong `args` slot, or writing the wrong counter, permutes those three words. The remaining fields are the constants 0, 1, 1, _, 1, 1, which distinguish the zero store at offset 0 from the memset's zeros around it. Buffer indices are the AIR `air.location_index` values 29 and 30, not the argument ordinals.

name: linked-single-fft-temp-write
rationale: One invocation selects one bounded FFT work item with unit extents and strides. The destination-temp path confines writes to the authored output allocation. The linked scalar prefix supplies exact one, the linked complex prefix supplies exact zero, and the linked postfix is inert.

name: keep-only-the-fragments-inside-a-scissor-rectangle-a-buffer-names
rationale:
The fragment is a hand-rolled scissor test: it discards unless position.x and position.y both lie between zero and the two components of a uint2 the constant buffer names. Four fcmp branches short-circuit into ONE shared discard block, which then falls through to the same return the fourth test reaches directly -- a five-predecessor convergence with no loop, which is the shape `native/cfg/blocks.rs` infers merges for and which the relooper then has to give a flow variable. Measured against every cased corpus source plus every public fixture, this 78-line module reaches 28 coverage rows (19 distinct functions) that nothing cased reaches: 20 rows in `cfg/blocks.rs` including `target_structured_merge`, `common_reachable_merge_after_header`, `conditional_merge_through_shared_body` and the whole `IndexedReachability` helper, plus `reloop_nest/emit.rs::emit_dispatch_header`/`flow_variable`/`widen_condition`/`flow_id_of` and `reloop_nest/verify.rs::definitely_written_on_entry`/`successors`.

`air.position` is the only stage input, so this fragment is fully determinate: reflection shows `varyings: []` and the coordinate is exactly (px+0.5, py+0.5). The extent buffer says (5, 3), so px+0.5 <= 5 is px <= 4 and py+0.5 <= 3 is py <= 2, and the surviving rectangle of the 8x8 target is the 5x3 block at the origin -- 15 pixels written 255 against 49 discarded. The rectangle is deliberately not square and not centred: swapping the two extent components, swapping position.x for position.y, or transposing the readback each moves 12 of the 15 written pixels.

Every one of the 64 initial texels is a DISTINCT value (0x1000 + py*8 + px), so a discarded fragment that writes anyway is caught at the exact pixel it wrote, and a surviving fragment that fails to write leaves a value that identifies itself. The two lower-bound tests (position.x < 0, position.y < 0) cannot fire for a rasterized fragment at any target size; they are structurally present in the CFG and are not device-discriminated by this case, and no case can discriminate them, because gl_FragCoord is never negative.

name: visible-table-clear-slots-two-through-seventeen-simd-primary
rationale: One invocation calls visible-function-table slots 2 through 17 and receives exact float4 zero from all sixteen linked _uber_clear bodies. A nineteen-word size table and eight explicit argument-info records keep every selector and offset in bounds; register 2 is selected. The entry writes that result to the poisoned primary texel before subgroup aggregation, and binding zero is captured byte-exactly.

name: domain-points-of-distinct-integer-edge-and-inside-factors-of-a-quad-patch
rationale: DESIGN D195 (K7b), restated in D208 to read the domain points instead of their interpolation: one quad patch with edge factors 1, 2, 3, 4 and inside factors 5, 2 under integer partitioning, drawn with rasterization disabled. The post-tessellation function marks the cell (rint(u * 20), rint(v * 18)) of a 65 x 65 word grid for each domain point it is called with (filled 0xAB, a mark is 1; the store is idempotent, so a point evaluated more than once marks once), and the case observes the marks only. The grid scales are per-patch attributes chosen so that no two of the 14 points share a cell and every point lies at least 0.024 of the domain from a cell boundary, far beyond any device's rounding of a coordinate. Integer partitioning spaces every edge and the inside grid equally, which Metal and Vulkan both fix, so every mark is pinned. The marks differ for every other assignment of the four edge factors to the edges, for the two inside factors swapped, for a mirrored domain, and under either fractional partitioning: which factor drives which edge and inside direction. The kernel also stores each point's raw coordinates after the marks; the case does not observe them, since neither API pins their bits (D208).

name: domain-points-of-fractional-even-partitioning-of-fractional-quad-factors
rationale: DESIGN D195 (K7b), restated in D208 to read the domain points instead of their interpolation: one quad patch with the fractional edge factors 2.5, 3.25, 1.75, 5.5 and inside factors 2.25, 4.75 under fractional even partitioning, which rounds them up to 4, 4, 2, 6 and 4, 6 segments, drawn with rasterization disabled. The post-tessellation function marks the cell (rint(u * 32), rint(v * 32)) of a 65 x 65 word grid for each domain point it is called with (filled 0xAB, a mark is 1; the store is idempotent, so a point evaluated more than once marks once), and the case observes the marks only. The grid scales are per-patch attributes chosen so that no two of the 31 points share a cell and every point lies at least 0.015 of the domain from a cell boundary, far beyond any device's rounding of a coordinate. Metal and Vulkan fix each edge's and ring's segment count and that the two shorter segments sit symmetrically; where they sit Vulkan leaves to the implementation, so these marks read the placement of D3D11's reference tessellator, which Apple's and Mesa's both follow bit for bit (D208). The counts alone already separate the three partition modes. The marks differ under integer and fractional odd partitioning of the same factors, for any other assignment of the edge factors, for the inside factors swapped, and for a mirrored domain. The kernel also stores each point's raw coordinates after the marks; the case does not observe them, since neither API pins their bits (D208).

name: domain-points-of-fractional-odd-partitioning-of-fractional-quad-factors
rationale: DESIGN D195 (K7b), restated in D208 to read the domain points instead of their interpolation: one quad patch with the fractional edge factors 2.5, 3.25, 1.75, 5.5 and inside factors 2.25, 4.75 under fractional odd partitioning, which rounds them up to 3, 5, 3, 7 and 3, 5 segments, drawn with rasterization disabled. The post-tessellation function marks the cell (rint(u * 23), rint(v * 56.125)) of a 65 x 65 word grid for each domain point it is called with (filled 0xAB, a mark is 1; the store is idempotent, so a point evaluated more than once marks once), and the case observes the marks only. The grid scales are per-patch attributes chosen so that no two of the 26 points share a cell and every point lies at least 0.0059 of the domain from a cell boundary, far beyond any device's rounding of a coordinate. Metal and Vulkan fix each edge's and ring's segment count and that the two shorter segments sit symmetrically; where they sit Vulkan leaves to the implementation, so these marks read the placement of D3D11's reference tessellator, which Apple's and Mesa's both follow bit for bit (D208). The counts alone already separate the three partition modes. The marks differ under integer and fractional even partitioning of the same factors, for any other assignment of the edge factors, for the inside factors swapped, and for a mirrored domain. The kernel also stores each point's raw coordinates after the marks; the case does not observe them, since neither API pins their bits (D208).

name: domain-points-of-integer-partitioning-of-fractional-quad-factors
rationale: DESIGN D195 (K7b), restated in D208 to read the domain points instead of their interpolation: one quad patch with the fractional edge factors 2.5, 3.25, 1.75, 5.5 and inside factors 2.25, 4.75 under integer partitioning, which rounds them up to 3, 4, 2, 6 and 3, 5 segments, drawn with rasterization disabled. The post-tessellation function marks the cell (rint(u * 24), rint(v * 30)) of a 65 x 65 word grid for each domain point it is called with (filled 0xAB, a mark is 1; the store is idempotent, so a point evaluated more than once marks once), and the case observes the marks only. The grid scales are per-patch attributes chosen so that no two of the 23 points share a cell and every point lies at least 0.016 of the domain from a cell boundary, far beyond any device's rounding of a coordinate. Integer partitioning spaces every edge and the inside grid equally, which Metal and Vulkan both fix, so every mark is pinned.
